learning_outcomes.text: Generic knowledge of Manufacturing Engineering, as well as mechanical manufacturing processes and their location in the productive context.
Ability to characterize the different elements of manufacturing processes.
Aptitude for identifying different mechanical manufacturing processes and their characteristics for establishing classifications and systematic studies thereof.
Knowledge of machine tools, tools, and fixtures for the main manufacturing processes.
Knowledge of the automation of machine tools using numerical control techniques.
Knowledge of the basics of Metrology and the application of metrological techniques in manufacturing.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of Quality and the implementation of standardized quality systems in production processes.
Knowledge of the different welding processes, as well as the equipment and consumables used in welded joints and their symbology.

syllabus_topics: Shaping by powder metallurgy techniques and rapid prototyping.
Shaping processes for polymeric and composite materials.
Mechanical assembly. Threaded joints. Riveted joints, etc.
Material removal processes. Numerical Control machine tools.
Other mechanical manufacturing processes. Laser beam machining. Electron beam machining. Water jet machining. Abrasive jet machining, etc.
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes using audiovisual aids (presentations, web pages).
Practical classes solving problems and exercises.
Field practices (visits to industries and centers of interest).
Use of AI tools for text improvement, review, and style enhancement, with proper referencing and verification.
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is the default, but students can opt for a single final assessment. For continuous assessment, a minimum score of 5.0 points is required in each partial exam. If the minimum is met in each partial, the total weighted score must also be 5.0 or higher to pass. If a partial is not passed, it can be recovered during the first official call; if both are failed, the entire course must be retaken. The continuous assessment scheme (90% partials + 10% reports) is maintained for all calls during the academic year. Students opting for the single assessment mode will take one final exam counting for 100% of the final grade.
